content.overview: Pre-use checks help catch obvious equipment problems before they create injury, crop loss, poor process performance or unnecessary downtime.

vocabulary.definition: A defined inspection performed before operating equipment to confirm obvious readiness and safety conditions.
A condition that must be met before an asset is used for the assigned task.
A controlled status indicating equipment should not be used until authorized evaluation or release.

sections.title: Check the asset before use
sections.body: Routine checks may include asset identity, cleanliness, visible damage, leaks, hoses or connections, guards, protective features, indicators and other steps defined by the equipment manufacturer or facility procedure. The exact checklist depends on the asset.

sections.title: Do not bypass protective features
sections.body: A missing guard, damaged cord, abnormal leak, unsafe condition or other failed readiness criterion triggers the facility's out-of-service or escalation process. Finishing the task is not justification for bypassing a protective device.

workedExamples: A leaking irrigation connection is handled only through the approved operator response or maintenance escalation.
A missing guard prevents use even if the operator believes careful technique would avoid contact.
commonMistakes: Skipping checks because equipment worked on the previous shift.
Using an improvised repair in place of an authorized maintenance decision.
content.practicalApplication: Perform a simulated pre-use inspection and classify findings as acceptable, routine operator correction, out-of-service/escalation or emergency hazard.
content.summary: Technicians verify equipment readiness before use and refuse to bypass failed safeguards, damaged equipment or authorization boundaries.
